A support bundle is always created locally on a crash. This switch only controls whether it is automatically uploaded to Google Drive - manual sharing/export is unaffected.

Creates and uploads a lightweight bundle with metrics (reconnects, error counts, DB growth) once a day so slowly developing problems become visible over time - Wi-Fi only, and only if something changed since the last one.

Automatically moves old recordings to trash (favorites are protected)

%1$d recordings older than %2$d days (%3$s) would be moved to the trash automatically from now on. Favorites and labeled recordings are excluded. They stay restorable from the trash for another 30 days.
Save database and settings to a file

Writes all recordings, sessions and settings to a ZIP file at a location of your choice (e.g. Google Drive, local storage). Replaces the previous adb-based instructions - no terminal needed. Note: the backup file contains the alerting credentials (ntfy) in plain text, so keep it as safe as any other export.
This replaces ALL current recordings, sessions and settings with the content of the selected backup file. This cannot be undone. The app will restart automatically afterwards.

1. Smartphone Microphone: Quick start, uncalibrated dB comparison value.\n\n2. PCE-323 via Bluetooth BLE: Standard-compliant, calibrated dBA measurement for official reports.
Important: Smartphone microphones are uncalibrated. For official verification we recommend the PCE-323.

The app requests permissions specifically when needed:
• Microphone: for audio recordings
• Bluetooth: for PCE-323 connection
• Notifications: for background service
To keep background monitoring running uninterrupted for hours, the app should be exempted from Android battery optimization.

A device that is not a sound level meter delivers no readings. The app then keeps retrying for about three minutes, reports “Failed” and starts a fresh attempt every 15 minutes.
